outcome: Help research teams identify potentially eligible participants and assemble protocol evidence faster while preserving consent, clinician judgement, and research governance.
overview: Trial protocols carry dozens of interacting eligibility criteria, and the records that answer them sit across notes, labs, imaging reports and pathology systems — so coordinators screen slowly, sites miss accrual targets and patients never hear about options they might have qualified for. This solution translates an approved protocol into reviewable, versioned criteria, searches governed clinical and research data under de-identification, and returns candidates in which every criterion is traced to its evidence or explicitly marked unknown. Investigators confirm or reject each candidate, and contact happens only through approved consent pathways. A trial pilot targets a 40% reduction in prescreening time.

benefits.text: Reduce coordinator prescreening time by a target 40% on the piloted protocol
benefits.limits: Basis: hypothesis. Target to validate against timed coordinator baselines on the customer’s own protocol — not a guarantee

benefits.text: Improve reviewed candidate yield so investigators spend review time on genuinely plausible participants
benefits.limits: Basis: hypothesis. Yield depends on record depth and terminology coverage; the solution never determines eligibility, and no enrolment or recruitment outcome is guaranteed

benefits.text: Trace every criterion decision to its evidence, with 100% investigator confirmation before any patient contact
benefits.source: Reference architecture criterion-tracing and consent design, Redington Healthcare catalogue,
benefits.limits: A design property of the review and consent workflow, verified in UAT and ethics review; not a claim about criterion accuracy

residency: Deployable in-country on local AWS or Azure regions (e.g. UAE, KSA); identifiable clinical data stays in the customer tenancy and candidate search runs against de-identified data in the reference designs, in line with UAE and Saudi health-data regulations and cross-border research rules

notFor.situation: No ethics approval or lawful basis for screening access to patient records
notFor.why: Screening identifiable records without an approved protocol, waiver or consent basis is a research-governance breach, not a recruitment technique

notFor.situation: Expectation that the solution determines eligibility or guarantees enrolment
notFor.why: The source catalogue makes no clinical eligibility or enrolment guarantee; eligibility is an investigator decision on the full record and the solution only proposes reviewable candidates

notFor.situation: Direct-to-patient outreach outside approved communication pathways
notFor.why: Unapproved contact risks therapeutic misconception and breaches the consent conditions the ethics committee set

scope:
Model: Joint delivery: accredited implementation partner leads, with Redington architecture and commercial governance; the customer owns ethics approval, protocol interpretation and investigator confirmation · Duration: 8–14-week pilot; 16–28 weeks to network deployment
Delivery pod: Partner delivery lead + project manager, clinical-informatics engineer, integration engineer, data scientist; customer research director, principal investigator, trial coordinator, ethics and privacy reviewers, EHR and CTMS integration leads · Support model: Business-hours or 24×7 option; severity-based response targets; partner service desk with vendor escalation
1) Protocol, ethics and data-access discovery
2) Data integration with de-identification and terminology mapping
3) Criteria normalisation and gold-set evaluation with investigators
4) Privacy, ethics and security review of the screening workflow
5) Controlled trial pilot with weekly recruitment and deviation review
6) Stabilisation, benefit review and handover

De-identification, contact-boundary and audit controls pass privacy and ethics review
CTMS and research-system reconciliation complete; coordinators complete UAT
languages: English delivery; English protocol and criteria handling, with Arabic source-document processing assessed per corpus
